newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls on Manila to release detained fishermen.
newsitem.headline: China calls on Manila to release detained fishermen.

text.p: China on Thursday called on the Philippines to release 21 fishermen seized near a disputed South China Sea shoal, saying Manila had seriously infringed on Chinese sovereignty.
"The Philippines side... has seriously infringed on Chinese sovereignty," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai told a news briefing.

The fishermen were arrested on May 20 off Scarborough Shoal, a 16-km (10-mile) rock formation which Manila says is within its 200-mile exclusive economic zone. Beijing says the shoal and other islets, reefs and rocks in the South China Sea are Chinese territory.
"We request the Philippines side to quickly release the people and the boats," Cui said, adding the fishermen had been engaging in routine fishing activities.
China has previously protested to the Philippines over the incident, demanding release of the fishermen.
Philippine President Fidel Ramos has said the fishermen would not be freed immediately. Philippine police said on Thursday that they had filed charges of illegal entry against them.
